item.title: Lakers ride 39-point 3rd quarter to surge past Clippers
item.description: Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers on Friday. Walker Kessler scored 22 points, Ziaire Williams contributed 14, while Matisse Thybulle and Quentin Grimes each had 13 as the Lakers won for the ninth time in their past 13 games against the cross-town Clippers. Kessler hit 10 of 14 shots from the floor and is now 22 of 26 over two games with his new team after a trade from the Utah Jazz in July. The Lakers had 13 steals and forced the Clippers into 26 turnovers that they turned into 33 points. Doncic committed 11 turnovers, while Kessler and Grimes led all rebounders with eight apiece. Darius Garland scored 26 points and Brook Lopez added 22 as the Clippers dropped their first road game of the season. Derrick Jones Jr. and Rui Hachimura each scored 16 points. The Clippers shot 49.4% from the floor and 43.2% from 3-point range but lost as the Lakers shot 58.2% from the floor and 43.8% from distance. The Lakers led 77-76 with 7:18 remaining in the third quarter when a 3-pointer from Thybulle kicked off a 14-1 run that gave them a 91-77 lead with 3:43 remaining in the period. The Lakers took a 103-90 lead into the fourth quarter after scoring 39 points in the third while shooting 72.7% from the floor. The Clippers used an 8-0 run to pull within 119-113 on a 3-pointer from Garland with 3:21 to play before Grimes sealed the victory on two free throws with 40.9 seconds remaining for a 125-117 lead. The Clippers led 31-27 after one quarter and went up by as many as 11 points less than three minutes into the second before the Lakers closed the gap. A three-point play by Doncic with 5.6 seconds remaining tied the game 64-64 at the half. Doncic led all scorers with 16 points before the break. --Field Level Media

item.title: Alperen Sengun, Rockets win physical battle against rival Spurs
item.description: Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as the Houston Rockets ground out a 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday in Austin, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as the Houston Rockets ground out a 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday in Austin, Texas. The Rockets led by two at halftime and by four after three quarters. San Antonio rallied to take a 104-103 lead on Dylan Harper's 3-pointer with 4:19 remaining. Houston kept feeding Sengun, who battled inside for a layups, two free throws and a three-point play on three consecutive possessions to put the Rockets ahead 109-104. Harper's emphatic dunk with 46.1 seconds left brought the Spurs within 112-110, and two defensive stops gave San Antonio one final chance with five seconds remaining. The Spurs went to Victor Wembanyama deep in the lane for the tying basket, but Amen Thompson blocked his layup above the rim. Fred VanVleet grabbed the rebound for Houston with 0.6 seconds remaining and sank two free throws to seal the win, the Rockets' second straight to open the season. Kevin Durant and Thompson added 20 points apiece for Houston, with Thompson also collecting 10 rebounds. VanVleet finished with 14 points, and Tari Eason scored 12. Wembanyama paced the Spurs with 25 points and 13 rebounds. Harper had 20 points, De'Aaron Fox added 19 points and nine assists, Stephon Castle tallied 15 points, and Devin Vassell scored 10 for San Antonio, which has opened the season with consecutive losses. Thompson's dunk capped a late Rockets run that gave Houston a 32-27 lead after the first quarter. Houston extended its advantage to 11 points, but the Spurs rallied to tie the game at 56 on Julian Champagnie's 3-pointer with 54.2 seconds left before halftime. The teams then traded baskets before VanVleet sank a 3-pointer at the buzzer to give the Rockets a 61-59 lead at the break. Wembanyama led all scorers and rebounders in the first half with 17 points and seven rebounds. Fox added 10 points. Sengun and Thompson paced Houston with 11 points apiece, while Durant scored 10. The Rockets led by as many as 10 in the third quarter. San Antonio responded with a Champagnie 3-pointer and a pair of free throws from Vassell to pull within four heading into the fourth. --Field Level Media

item.title: ATP roundup: Alexander Bublik survives thriller to reach Almaty semis
item.description: Third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan rallied past fifth-seeded Russian Karen Khachanov 4-6, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) in Friday's Almaty Open quarterfinals in Kazakhstan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan rallied past fifth-seeded Russian Karen Khachanov 4-6, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) in Friday's Almaty Open quarterfinals in Kazakhstan. Bublik hammered 21 aces and finished with 49 winners in his first match of the tournament after advancing via a second-round walkover. Khachanov secured the only service break of the match in the opening set, but Bublik responded by winning both ensuing tiebreakers. He will face top-seeded Daniil Medvedev, who reached the semifinals with a 6-4, 6-4 victory over France's Terence Atmane. Medvedev did not face a break point and won 91% of his first-serve points. Seventh-seeded Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece also advanced in straight sets, defeating Australia's James Duckworth 6-3, 6-4. Tsitsipas fired 15 aces, did not face a break point and won 34 of 37 first-serve points. He will meet qualifier Nikoloz Basilashvili after the Georgian rolled past France's Adrian Mannarino 6-3, 6-1. BNP Paribas Fortis European Open Top-seeded Arthur Fils of France fought off fifth-seeded American Alex Michelsen 6-4, 7-6 (12) to advance to the semifinals in Brussels. Fils needed six match points to finally close out the 14-12 second-set tiebreaker. He won 79% of his first-serve points, recorded six aces and converted three of four break chances in the one-hour, 50-minute match. He will face Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff, who ended Belgium's hopes of a home semifinalist by defeating No. 6 seed Zizou Bergs 6-3, 7-6 (6). The Netherlands' Tallon Griekspoor rallied to eliminate No. 2 Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic 4-6, 6-4, 6-3. Griekspoor converted three of four break points and overcame Lehecka's 11 aces to reach his second semifinal of the season. He will play third-seeded Francisco Cerundolo after the Argentine dispatched French qualifier Clement Chidekh 6-2, 6-4. Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes Second-seeded Taylor Fritz topped Germany's Daniel Altmaier 7-6 (5), 6-2 to set up an all-American semifinal at the ATP 250 event in Lyon, France. Fritz beat Altmaier for the first time in three career meetings. He will next face No. 4 seed Tommy Paul, who needed two hours, 45 minutes to subdue France's Corentin Moutet 6-4, 3-6, 6-3. Paul converted five of 10 break point chances and saved 10 of 14 opportunities. Top-seeded Flavio Cobolli of Italy recovered from a set down to defeat fifth-seeded Brandon Nakashima 4-6, 6-4, 6-4. Cobolli will meet countryman Lorenzo Musetti after the No. 6 seed survived another lengthy quarterfinal, edging France's Luca Van Assche 7-6 (5), 6-7 (7), 6-4 in three hours, 33 minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bolsonaro and Lula clash on living costs, corruption in final Brazil election debate
item.description: Opinion polls have shown the two about even before Sunday's presidential runoff.
item.dc:creator: Andre Romani
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks on Friday in the last presidential debate before Sunday's runoff, as both candidates sought to win over undecided voters amid a tight race. Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, led Lula in the first round of the election earlier this month, but opinion polls have shown the two candidates [USN:L1N4681FZ TEXT:"about even"] this week after the gap between them narrowed. Bolsonaro and Lula repeated their campaign proposals during the over two-hour debate hosted by Globo, Brazil's most-watched TV channel, focusing on themes such as the cost of living, welfare and security, while exchanging allegations of corruption. Lula, who is seeking his fourth term after winning back the presidency in 2022, has defended his government's above-inflation minimum wage increases and stressed that his administration helped millions of Brazilians to escape hunger. The president said the younger Bolsonaro "is like students studying for college entrance exams. They can memorize things, but they can't learn." He also said that "in the gated community where Bolsonaro lives, people don't go hungry." Bolsonaro responded by saying food prices for Brazilians rose during Lula's administration, and he criticized a tax reform approved by the current government, projecting the new rules would raise the tax burden on consumers. "Lula doesn't even remember the last time he went grocery shopping because he lives in a luxury palace now." The two candidates mostly limited the discussion to pre-established themes in the first few segments of the debate, toning down the [USN:L6N46406G TEXT:"personal attacks"] that marked the only previous debate in the campaign between the two. At one point, Bolsonaro apologized to Lula after saying the president gives to Brazilians with one hand but "takes away with nine fingers." Lula lost his left little finger in an accident while working as a lathe operator in a factory. "I will not accept some rich guy, with a highly questionable political practice, calling me 'nine fingers,'" the incumbent said, demanding a retraction. "Lula, if I offended you by calling you 'nine fingers,' then I sincerely apologize, I sincerely apologize," Bolsonaro said. But he added: "Will you apologize to Brazilians suffering from insecurity ... in debt?" The discussion heated up in the last minutes of the debate, when both candidates were allowed to interact without moderation, as Lula and Bolsonaro sought to link each other to the fraud involving lender Banco Master. Lula pressed Bolsonaro on [USN:L1N4530F5 TEXT:"alleged links"] to the bank's jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula [USN:L1N43X02G TEXT:"about accusations"] involving his son and a pension fraud. The debate was one of the campaign's final events, as Brazilian electoral law bars the candidates from broadcasting radio and TV campaign advertising starting on Saturday. They can still hold rallies until the final hours of the day.

item.title: Jaren Jackson Jr., Jazz eke out home-opening win over Pelicans
item.description: Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally the Utah Jazz to a 120-119 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally the Utah Jazz to a 120-119 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday in Salt Lake City. Utah rookie Darryn Peterson scored 15 points, including two go-ahead free throws with 50.5 seconds left. Jaxson Hayes chipped in 17 points off the bench and Lauri Markkanen added 16 to help the Jazz beat the Pelicans for the first time since November 2023. New Orleans went 3-0 against Utah each of the previous two seasons and had won eight straight in the series. The Jazz earned the home-opening victory after dropping their overall opener on Wednesday at Memphis. Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 23 points and reserve Saddiq Bey added 20. Dejounte Murray chipped in 16. Murray missed a potential game-winning jumper with a second left as the Pelicans fell to 0-2. New Orleans center Yves Missi went to the locker room with 6:24 left in the second quarter after sustaining a left knee injury. Missi could not put any weight on his left leg as he was helped off the court. He tallied six points on 3-of-3 shooting in nine minutes. Even without Missi, New Orleans erased a 15-point deficit in the third quarter and took its first lead at 75-74 midway through the quarter on a reverse layup from Murray. The Pelicans scored on 10 consecutive possessions during the rally. Murray accounted for five baskets in that stretch. The Pelicans scored 38 points in the third quarter and carried that momentum into the fourth. Back-to-back baskets from Bennedict Mathurin and Bey helped New Orleans build its largest lead at 99-94. George drained a 3-pointer and fed Hayes for a floater, capping a 15-3 run that put the Jazz back in front 109-102 with 5:35 left. Utah dominated in the paint early to assert control. The Jazz scored 22 of their 31 first-quarter points in the paint. The Jazz never trailed before halftime and claimed a 40-30 lead early in the second quarter behind a 9-0 run. Markkanen and Brice Sensabaugh bookended the surge with 3-pointers. Utah eventually expanded its lead to 67-52 early in the third on another trey from Markkanen. --Field Level Media

item.title: Marquez wins thrilling Australian MotoGP sprint to retake championship lead
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez emerged victorious in an electrifying battle with championship rival Jorge Martin before going on to win the Australian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez emerged victorious in an electrifying battle with championship rival Jorge Martin before going on to win the Australian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead. Victory moved seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez up to 365 points in the championship standings, 10 points ahead of Martin, who did not finish the sprint after suffering a gruesome crash in the eighth lap. The reigning champion can further extend that lead in Sunday's race, with Martin declared unfit after breaking his wrist in the crash. After a couple of [USN:L4N4691TI TEXT:"wet qualifying sessions"] earlier in the day, the sprint began on a dry track at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit, with dark clouds looming overhead. Pole-sitter Marquez shot off the line and held on to his lead, though his start was matched by title rival Martin, who barrelled past Alex Marquez and Johann Zarco into second place from fourth. Without the rain to hinder him, Martin squeezed every ounce of pace he could out of his Aprilia on the circuit's swooping corners and stole the lead from Marquez three times, only to overplay his hand and quickly give it away on every occasion. The 2024 champion continued to push, and his overzealousness proved to be his undoing in the eighth lap, as his bike slid out from under him and he went hurtling into the gravel at high speed. "It was a title battle. Of course I gave everything. I was aggressive and he was faster than me, but I tried to defend in the best way possible," Marquez said after his win. "There were nice overtakes, limit overtakes. And in the end, both of us were riding on the limit. Both of us deserved the victory because we are pushing a lot. But, you know, racing is like it is. "Today, it was on my side, but, this (season) is super long, so, keep calm, keep going, and yeah, happy for today." MARTIN TO MISS RACE Martin was carried away from the site of the crash on a stretcher as Aprilia confirmed that he had been taken to the medical centre for evaluation. The Spaniard was later pictured walking out of the medical centre with his arm in a sling and his wrist wrapped up tightly. "Jorge Martin has been declared unfit to race after suffering a fracture to his right wrist! Wishing Jorge a speedy recovery," MotoGP said in a statement on social media. Martin will also be a doubt for next week's Malaysian Grand Prix. Trackhouse Aprilia rider Raul Fernandez, who won the Australian Grand Prix in 2025, was also ruled out of Sunday's race due to inflammation of tissue around a finger fracture that he sustained at the [USN:L1N45X01G TEXT:"Indonesian Grand Prix"] this month. "It’s not how I wanted to say goodbye to Phillip Island, but my finger has said it’s enough. I need to take a break and recover so I can come back at 100%," Fernandez said on social media. Marquez's brother Alex of Gresini Racing finished second, with Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Racing) completing the podium. "It was quite dramatic. For me, I had the best seat, sitting in the third place (behind Marc Marquez and Martin)," Alex said. Martin's teammate Marco Bezzecchi finished in fourth place, keeping his outside shot at winning the title alive. Home hero Jack Miller of Pramac Racing was eighth in the final sprint [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year.

item.title: Moonshot curbs hacking ability in new Kimi model as fears grow over AI-powered cyberattacks
item.description: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking. Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model. The company plans to publish the model's weights — files allowing outside developers to run and modify it on their own systems — by November 4. Moonshot said it removed cyber-related data from the training corpus and reinforcement-learning environments used to develop the model, while retaining general coding skills. "We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," the company said. Governments, technology companies and security researchers are growing increasingly concerned that AI could make sophisticated hacking easier and cheaper. Models that can write code, operate software tools and complete long, multi-step tasks may help users identify weaknesses in programs and automate parts of cyberattacks. China [USN:L1N46209C TEXT:"proposed export controls"] last week that would ban exports of AI-driven malware-generation and mutation technology and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability-discovery tools. The draft measures, which remain open for public comment, cite the risk that such capabilities could be used against critical infrastructure, defence-industrial and core government systems, or to bypass security protections. Moonshot said open-weight models can improve security by helping more organisations inspect and secure their own software, including older systems that receive little attention. Unlike proprietary, closed-weight AI systems, however, open-weight releases make central oversight more difficult. Once the files are widely distributed, the original developer has less ability to restrict access, monitor use or update safeguards than with a hosted service. K3.1 Pro scored 81.0% on its internal cyber benchmark, compared with 90.5% for a similar version without the risk-reduction measures, the company said. The test involved finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor. The results have not been independently verified. K3.1 Pro has a 1-million-token context window, allowing it to process very large amounts of text at once. Moonshot also released a faster version, K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it said runs at two to three times the speed of the standard model.

item.title: Nathan MacKinnon's 4-point night powers Avs past Lightning
item.description: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Mackenzie Blackwood turned away 31 shots, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 in Denver on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Mackenzie Blackwood turned away 31 shots, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 in Denver on Friday night. Martin Necas had a goal and two assists, Artturi Lehkonen and Devon Toews each collected a goal and an assist, and Nazem Kadri and Fedor Svechkov also scored for Colorado, which snapped a two-game skid. Jake Guentzel scored twice, Charle-Edouard D'Astous added a goal and an assist, Brayden Point had two assists, and Andrei Vasilevskiy made 18 saves for Tampa Bay, which had its three-game winning streak snapped. Toews gave Colorado the early lead when Necas fed him with a cross-ice pass, and he beat Vasilevskiy with a wrist shot 1:08 after the opening faceoff. Kadri made it 2-0 on the power play at 5:52 of the first period, taking a pass from T.J. Hughes in the slot and scoring with a snap shot. The Avalanche extended their lead to 3-0 just 24 seconds into the second period when Svechkov's pass attempt in front of the net deflected off a sprawling Erik Cernak. Svechkov then tapped the puck out of the air and into the net. The Lightning got on the board during one of their five power-play opportunities in the second period when Guentzel scored on a rebound at 8:13. Lehkonen made it 4-1 at 13:57, converting a centering pass from MacKinnon. Tampa Bay answered at the end of another power play when Guentzel stuffed home a pass from Point at 19:17 of the second period. Colorado unsuccessfully challenged the play for a missed stoppage, giving the Lightning another power play. MacKinnon restored Colorado's three-goal lead at 4:18 of the third period. He took a pass from Lehkonen in the neutral zone, skated in on Vasilevskiy and buried a shot inside the near post. D'Astous cut the deficit to 5-3 at 15:13. Vasilevskiy came off for an extra attacker with less than three minutes remaining, and Necas scored into the empty net seconds later. Avalanche forward Logan O'Connor made his season debut, recording three shots in nearly 15 minutes of ice time. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers survive harrowing 9th to edge Rays in World Series opener
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers closer Trevor Megill wasn't perfect, but he was good enough to give Milwaukee a one-game advantage in the World Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers closer Trevor Megill wasn't perfect, but he was good enough to give Milwaukee a one-game advantage in the World Series. Hard-throwing ace Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run over five gritty innings and Megill stranded the tying run at third base to preserve the Brewers' 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night in the opening game of the World Series. Milwaukee, whose only other World Series appearance was a seven-game loss in 1982, scored two runs in the first inning off Nick Martinez and added a run in the seventh on Jackson Chourio's RBI single to go up 3-1. The Rays scored one run in the ninth off Megill, who entered to start the inning and conceded consecutive one-out singles to Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson. Pinch runner Jorge Mateo and Simpson executed a double steal, and Junior Caminero walked to load the bases. Liam Hicks appeared to bounce into a game-ending double play, but a video review showed that shortstop Cooper Pratt was pulled off the bag at second on the throw by second baseman Brice Turang. Hicks was out on the fielder's choice as Mateo scored to make it 3-2, leaving runners on second and third. Megill then struck out Jonny DeLuca for his fifth postseason save in five opportunities. "A lot of times those plays stand during the year, but I'm sure now they have every angle, and they took their time and got it right." Brewers manager Pat Murphy said of the review. "Megill kept his composure. We talk about it all the time. When there's a challenge, do not walk off the mound. Kept his composure, and that was the biggest at-bat of the game." Misiorowski (1-0), whose 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts each led the majors during the regular season, allowed one run on four hits in five innings. He fanned three and walked one in a 78-pitch outing. Misiorowski set the tone by throwing a 103.5 mph fastball to open the game, the fastest pitch in World Series history. "I thought Miz was great tonight," Murphy said. "What we're used to seeing in the regular season was Miz just mow through people and have two strikeouts an inning. That's unrealistic. This is the best team in the American League. They proved that during the regular season and proved that in the postseason so far. One of the ways they do that is to make contact better than anybody in baseball." Afterward, the 24-year-old Milwaukee ace was trying to process his first World Series appearance. "I still don't know how I felt. I feel like I'm still trying to take everything in and understand what happened," Misiorowski said. "Obviously went out and did my best and did enough for the team to get a win. That's all I can ask for." After Misiorowski's exit, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined for three scoreless innings, striking out five. "We came up a little bit short, but there's some benefit maybe from a loss," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "We saw Ashby. We saw Uribe. We saw Megill. I'd like to think that's going to help us moving forward a little bit." The Brewers posted two quick runs against Martinez (1-1), who got the start when ace Drew Rasmussen was pushed back to Game 2 for an extra day's rest. Chourio singled on the first pitch and scored on Christian Yelich's one-out triple off DeLuca's glove on a diving catch attempt in right-center. William Contreras followed with an RBI single to left. The Rays got a run back in the fourth. Aranda drew a leadoff walk and advanced to third when center fielder Garrett Mitchell misplayed Caminero's 112.7 mph drive into a double. He scored on Hicks' groundout. The Brewers made it 3-1 in the seventh. Steven Matz walked Pratt, who advanced on a groundout and scored on Chourio's two-out single down the right field line against Kevin Kelly. Martinez allowed two runs on five hits in five innings, striking out five and walking none. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Mavericks awaiting update on star Cooper Flagg (shoulder)
item.description: The prognosis for Dallas forward Cooper Flagg, who exited the Mavericks' Friday game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis due to left shoulder soreness, was unclear following the contest.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The prognosis for Dallas forward Cooper Flagg, who exited the Mavericks' Friday game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis due to left shoulder soreness, was unclear following the contest. "He'll be evaluated in the next couple of days," Mavericks coach Dusty May said. As for whether Flagg would require an MRI, May added, "I really don't know. I saw him in the locker room, he's in good spirits. We'll know in the next couple days what's next." Flagg, the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year, took a hard foul late in the second quarter and did not return to action. With 59.7 seconds left in the first half, Indiana's Aaron Nesmith challenged Flagg's dunk attempt from behind, sending Flagg sprawling to the floor. After a review, Nesmith was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Naji Marshall rushed in and shoved Nesmith, resulting in technical fouls for both players. Dallas carried a 77-43 lead into the locker room. "Nesmith's a great guy," May said following the Mavericks' 121-105 win. "Heck of a player. I've known him since he was in high school. An unfortunate play. Hopefully Coop's fine, but obviously it's something we wish wouldn't have happened." Flagg notched 14 points, six assists and five rebounds in 17 minutes of first-half play before being ruled out. The 19-year-old registered 32 points and five rebounds in the Mavericks' season-opening loss to the Houston Rockets. He averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 70 games last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fire devastates former Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest'
item.description: Firefighters battled for hours to contain a blaze that engulfed the former Nazi guest house known as "The Eagle's Nest" in southern Germany, while police investigated the cause after detaining a man near the scene, authorities said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Firefighters battled for hours to contain a blaze that engulfed the former Nazi guest house known as "The Eagle's Nest" in southern Germany, while police investigated the cause after detaining a man near the scene, authorities said on Saturday. Around 200 firefighters and emergency workers near Berchtesgaden in Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said. Built in 1938 as a guest house for Nazi officials and their guests, the building sits in a spectacular Alpine setting above Berchtesgaden. Adolf Hitler used it occasionally, earning it the nickname "Hitler's Tea House". It is separate from his nearby summer residence, the Berghof. Bild newspaper quoted a police spokesperson as saying the building, preserved after World War Two as a historical monument linked to the Nazi era, had been so badly damaged that it "could probably not be saved". Police said earlier they had detained a man near the site but had not yet established the cause of the fire. "Whether the person is linked to the fire is currently the subject of a criminal investigation," Bavarian police said in a statement.

item.title: Jake Evans tallies twice, adds assist as Canadiens topple Blackhawks
item.description: Jake Evans produced two goals and an assist and Jacob Fowler stopped 20 shots, lifting the visiting Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jake Evans produced two goals and an assist and Jacob Fowler stopped 20 shots, lifting the visiting Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Friday. Kaiden Guhle added a goal and assist to help Montreal earn its first road victory since opening night. Mike Matheson also scored as the Canadiens improved to 4-1-1 in their past six games. Connor Bedard scored and Spencer Knight made 24 saves as the Blackhawks fell to 2-3-0 on a seven-game homestand. Chicago started strong, as Bedard opened the scoring at 4:23 of the first period on a snap shot from just outside the left circle. After a Montreal dump-in glanced off a linesman, Patrick Kane collected the puck and slid it to a streaking Bedard in the neutral zone for his second goal this season. Montreal, playing without captain and top center Nick Suzuki (upper body), struggled to find offensive footing in the early going. The Canadiens needed 3:31 to record their first shot on goal and didn't register another for another 2 1/2 minutes. Evans tallied the equalizer at 17:29 of the first period with his first goal of the season, beating Knight with a wrist shot from in front of the net off a feed from Kirby Dach. Montreal took the lead on Evans' short-handed goal at 7:45 of the second period. With the Canadiens pressuring the Blackhawks' five-forward power play, a Kane shot attempt redirected off Tyler Bertuzzi's skate and created an odd-man rush for Montreal. Evans carried the puck down the left side and scored from the circle. Fowler turned aside Roman Kantserov and Kane on a Chicago rush moments later to preserve a one-goal advantage. The Canadiens made it 3-1 at 18:26 of the second. Guhle netted his first goal of the season on a wrist shot from the point. Chicago finished 0-for-5 on the power play compared to 0-for-3 for Montreal. The Blackhawks' final man advantage of the game lasted just 22 seconds in the third period, as Teuvo Teravainen was whistled for interference moments after Montreal's Juraj Slafkovsky was penalized for hooking. Matheson's empty-net goal, his first tally of the season, at 17:22 accounted for the final margin. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pistons jump out to big lead, hand Heat second straight loss
item.description: John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds, and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 128-111 victory over the host Miami Heat on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds, and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 128-111 victory over the host Miami Heat on Friday night. The Pistons (2-0) led wire to wire after scoring the game's first 11 points and built a lead of as many as 23 in the third quarter. The Heat (0-2) never got closer than eight points after Detroit's early surge despite another strong outing from Giannis Antetokounmpo. Antetokounmpo scored a game-high 36 points, grabbed 12 rebounds and dished out five assists for his first double-double in a Miami uniform. Collins, who shot 5-of-6 from 3-point range, helped Detroit build a 22-5 lead and spearheaded a 47.4% effort from beyond the arc (18-of-38). The Pistons shot 52.8% from the field (47-of-89), with former Heat guard Duncan Robinson making five of 10 3-point attempts and finishing with 17 points. It was another subpar defensive effort for Miami, which allowed 21 3-pointers and 131 points in its season-opening loss to Minnesota on Wednesday. The Heat were hampered in the first half when Bam Adebayo picked up three fouls in the first quarter and sat with 1:13 remaining. Adebayo did not return until the start of the second half. He finished with just four points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals before fouling out. Detroit's Cade Cunningham committed seven turnovers but finished with 16 points and eight assists. Daniss Jenkins scored 15 points, while Isaiah Joe chipped in 12. Miami made 15 3-pointers but shot just 29.4% from long range on 51 attempts. Davion Mitchell totaled 18 points and five rebounds, while Bobby Portis Jr. had 11 points and eight rebounds. The Heat shot just 38.2% from the field. Pistons center Jalen Duren left with 6:45 remaining in the second quarter due to a right thigh injury and did not return. He finished with four points and six rebounds in 10 minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: US accuses government contractor of leaking classified info to girlfriend's Substack
item.description: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Trotta
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter. The FBI arrested Ian Brinksman, 42, on Friday following a search of his Washington home, a Justice Department statement said. Prosecutors charged him with unlawfully transmitting national defense information. A federal public defender representing Brinksman declined to comment. “As alleged, Brinksman reached far outside his own duties to obtain some of our Nation’s most closely held secrets and handed them to a romantic partner he knew intended to publish them,” John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for national security, said in the statement. “That is not carelessness. It is a betrayal of his oath and the American people who entrusted him to fulfill his duties honorably,” Eisenberg said. Brinksman held a top secret security clearance while working as an employee of a US government agency and later as a developer for systems integration for a private contractor working for the same agency, prosecutors said. According to the sworn affidavit of an FBI agent investigating the case, Brinksman repeatedly accessed classified intelligence reports and then communicated with the journalist. The affidavit also cites phone records, database access logs, badge-swipe records, emails and other evidence. The affidavit only identifies the journalist as "Individual 1," but it cites excerpts from articles she published. "A fundraising article reportedly published by Individual 1 in September 2026 stated 'over the past year [Individual 1 has] published reporting based on classified [relevant U.S. government agency] assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about,'" the affidavit reads. That quote appears in a September 28 piece published on the Capital & Empire online newsletter authored by Aída Chávez. "Over the past year, I’ve published reporting based on classified CIA assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about," wrote Chávez, whose profile on the site notes that she worked for The Nation and other outlets before she launched the newsletter. Chávez did not immediately respond to an email message seeking comment. Investigators allege that on at least five occasions in 2026, Individual 1 published Substack articles containing information that mirrored the classified reports, some at the top secret level. On some of those dates, Chávez published articles that cite classified reports, some of them attributed to the CIA. According to a LinkedIn profile bearing Brinksman's name, he worked for Deloitte as a manager and as a senior strategy security consultant after having worked as a US State Department foreign service officer at dates corresponding to those outlined in the Justice Department statement. Deloitte did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The State Department said it needed more time to respond before commenting.

item.title: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, leaving 1 dead, 500 injured
item.description: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there.
item.dc:creator: Yimou Lee, Angie Teo, Ann Wang
item.content:encoded: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kph (78 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. The storm was about 170 km (106 miles) northeast of Taiwan, having glanced off the island's northeastern coast in Yilan County early on Saturday, the CWA said. The centre of the storm turned south around midnight, hugging the Yilan coastline before making a rare loop offshore and moving away northward. Wind gusts touched 227 kph (141 mph) in some coastal areas, knocking down power lines and sending roof tiles flying. 'MOST TERRIFYING AROUND MIDNIGHT' "It was most terrifying around midnight," said a retired teacher surnamed Lin as he inspected downed banana trees in his garden in Yilan. "It was a sleepless night. I haven't seen anything like this in many years." The storm's forecast track shows it turning north, tracking up the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan. Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at 1, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain. Taipower said more than 288,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected. The transport ministry said 259 flights were cancelled, an improvement from Friday, when the number was almost 1,000. In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers. Taipei resident Thomas Wang, 70, said the storm felt like something out of the horror film "Poltergeist". "It was quite scary," he said, out running morning errands. Governments in a swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday. Although more common in summer, typhoons can strike in autumn too. China's emergency management ministry sent a team to the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. It said it had readied 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment, while more than 41,000 firefighters were on emergency duty. In Taizhou, a city on Zhejiang's coast, more than 3,800 fishing boats returned to harbour, offshore fish-farm workers were brought ashore and 2,084 island visitors were evacuated, state media reported. Authorities halted 25 offshore construction projects and suspended 18 passenger ferry routes.

item.title: Mavericks beat Pacers as Cooper Flagg leaves with shoulder soreness
item.description: Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as the Mavericks defeated the Indiana Pacers 121-105 on Friday in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Dallas' Cooper Flagg.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as the Mavericks defeated the Indiana Pacers 121-105 on Friday in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Dallas' Cooper Flagg. With 59.7 seconds left in the second quarter, Aaron Nesmith challenged Flagg's dunk attempt from behind, sending Flagg sprawling. After a review, Nesmith was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Naji Marshall rushed in and shoved Nesmith, and both players were assessed technical fouls. Dallas carried a 77-43 lead into the locker room, but Flagg, who had 14 points, five rebounds and six assists, did not return for the second half due to left shoulder soreness. P.J. Washington added 20 points and 13 rebounds for the Mavericks, while Max Christie scored 16, Marshall had 15 and Zaccharie Risacher contributed 11 points. Pascal Siakam paced Indiana with 23 points and Tyrese Haliburton, who missed all of last season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, added 18 points in his first home game in 491 days. Andrew Nembhard scored 16 points for the Pacers. Obi Toppin contributed 13 points, and Ivica Zubac grabbed 11 rebounds. Each team ended the game with a 1-1 record. Dallas built a 30-17 lead on a 14-2 run, capped by Irving's layup with 3:27 left in the first quarter. Irving and Flagg hit back-to-back threes, giving Dallas a 43-25 lead as the first quarter wound down. Dallas extended its lead to 50-31 when Marshall stole the ball from Siakam and fed Risacher for a one-handed dunk with 7:55 left in the second quarter. The Mavericks eventually stretched the margin to 30 points during a 15-0 run. Toppin's three-point play capped an 8-0 Pacers run that cut their deficit to 85-62 with 4:22 left in the third quarter. Toppin's dunk cut the deficit to 106-90 with 7:38 remaining, and Haliburton's jumper trimmed it to 118-105 with 1:56 left. Dallas finished without Irving, who fouled out with 4:23 to go. --Field Level Media

item.title: Scottie Barnes, RJ Barrett fuel Raptors past Wizards
item.description: Scottie Barnes collected 28 points and 14 rebounds and RJ Barrett added 23 and nine, respectively, lifting the visiting Toronto Raptors to a 112-102 victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Scottie Barnes collected 28 points and 14 rebounds and RJ Barrett added 23 and nine, respectively, lifting the visiting Toronto Raptors to a 112-102 victory over the Washington Wizards on Friday. Barnes made 12 of 26 shots from the floor to offset eight turnovers for the Raptors, who never trailed in the contest and improved to 2-0. Kawhi Leonard recorded 16 points and nine rebounds and Immanuel Quickley added 12 points and six assists for Toronto. The Raptors shot 43.6% from the floor and enjoyed a decisive 52-32 edge in points in the paint. Trae Young highlighted his 22-point, 12-assist performance by draining four 3-pointers, with his last cutting Washington's deficit to 94-89 with 8:04 to play. Toronto responded with an 11-3 run, with Barrett making a pair of driving layups and an 18-foot jumper in that stretch. Washington countered by scoring five straight points before Leonard made a pair of baskets and Barnes converted a three-point play to effectively seal the win. Kyshawn George had 11 points on 2-of-9 shooting while committing eight of the Wizards' 23 turnovers. Washington's AJ Dybantsa, the top overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, sat out his second straight game with a sprained left ankle as the Wizards fell to 1-1. Barnes' dunk extended Toronto's lead to 76-66 with 2:50 remaining in the third quarter before Young sank his third 3-pointer of the evening, igniting an 11-2 run. Justin Champagnie had a pair of layups and converted an alley-oop dunk during that sequence before Jamison Battle drilled a 3-pointer just before the end of the quarter for Toronto. The Raptors put the game on ice by outscoring the Wizards by a 31-25 margin in the fourth quarter. George sank a pair of free throws to cut Toronto's lead to 16-11 with 4:32 remaining in the first before the Raptors responded with an 18-10 run to end the quarter. Barnes drained two jumpers and a 3-pointer during the late surge. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hot-shooting Hawks set franchise mark with 47-point rout of Hornets
item.description: Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 on Friday, the biggest margin of victory in Hawks history.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 on Friday, the biggest margin of victory in Hawks history. The 47-point gap topped the old record of 46 points set in a 126-80 victory over the visiting Sacramento Kings on Nov 15, 2017. Nickeil Alexander-Walker put up 14 points, CJ McCollum posted 13 points, Dyson Daniels contributed 11 points and nine rebounds and Corey Kispert also had 11 points for Atlanta, which won its second game in a row to start the season. Onyeka Okongwu added 10 points as the Hawks shot 50.5% from the field. Johnson supplied eight assists. It was a miserable home opener for the Hornets, who won two nights earlier at Brooklyn to start their campaign. They committed 27 turnovers. Naz Reid scored 17 points for Charlotte and Grayson Allen came off the bench for 11 points. Both players were in their home debuts with the Hornets. Reserve Tidjane Salaun also scored 11 points. The Hawks were efficient on offense throughout the game. The gap reached 97-62 by the end of the third quarter. The Hornets couldn't even get it cranked up when the margin was out of hand, needing about 6 1/2 minutes to reach a double-digit total in the fourth quarter. Wiggins, who shot 7-for-9 from the field, hit 3 of 5 from 3-point range. Charlotte's Brandon Miller finished 2-for-14 from the field, including 1-for-11 on 3-point tries. He scored six points. The Hornets didn't apply much pressure, not attempting a 10th free throw until deep into the fourth quarter. Atlanta built a 15-point first-quarter lead. It was 33-20 through the opening quarter, with the Hornets willing to fire away from the perimeter. Charlotte was 2-for-15 on first-quarter 3-point attempts. The Hawks poured it on in the second quarter to claim a 68-43 halftime lead on the strength of Wiggins' 15 points along with 13 points apiece from Johnson and McCollum. Atlanta benefited from Charlotte's 14 first-half turnovers. The Hornets played again without injured Kon Knueppel (hamstring), Coby White (calf) and Grant Williams (hamstring). --Field Level Media

item.title: UK's Healey to give two state-backed lenders £20 billion capital boost in budget
item.description: British finance minister John Healey is expected to announce £20.4 billion ($27.3 billion) of additional support to the state's business lender and infrastructure bank in his budget on Wednesday, the Treasury said, confirming a newspaper report.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: British finance minister John Healey is expected to announce £20.4 billion ($27.3 billion) of additional support to the state's business lender and infrastructure bank in his budget on Wednesday, the Treasury said, confirming a newspaper report. The Treasury will allocate £15.4 billion ($20.6 billion) more to the National Wealth Fund and £5 billion ($7 billion) more to the British Business Bank over roughly half a decade "This additional capital will help more British businesses fulfil their potential, while getting investment behind the industries, infrastructure and places that create good jobs and drive lasting growth across the country," a Treasury spokesperson said in an emailed statement The Treasury said the funding would help support around 100,000 jobs by 2035 in sectors including artificial intelligence, defence and green energy The Financial Times first reported the news ($1 = 0.7478 pounds)

item.title: US has for years asked Musk to alter Starlink service in Ukraine, Middle East, sources say
item.description: The Biden-era and Trump requests to Musk show a close relationship in which US administrations rely to an unprecedented degree on a private-sector company to help implement foreign policy.
item.dc:creator: Erin Banco, Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: Well before the throttling this month of Ukraine's military access to Elon Musk's satellite communications system, the Biden and Trump administrations had several times asked SpaceX to turn its Starlink service on or off in various countries, according to six former senior US officials familiar with the matter. During the presidency of Joe Biden, the requests included switching off the service to prevent Iranian proxy militias in Yemen and Lebanon from using Starlink to communicate, and activating the service to provide internet access inside Iran and in Ukraine to support its military, said four of the former officials. Similarly, President Donald Trump's administration asked Musk, who is CEO of SpaceX, to make the service available in Iran following US-Israeli strikes in 2025 and 2026, in hopes it would bolster internet access and communications for anti-government protesters, a former senior Trump official and a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. All of the people spoke on condition of anonymity. The previous US requests about Starlink access are being reported here for the first time. The recent blowup over restrictions to Ukraine's use of SpaceX satellite services has raised questions about the ties between the US government and Musk, whose company owns systems vital to the US military and to US allies. The Biden-era and Trump requests to Musk show a close relationship in which US administrations rely to an unprecedented degree on a private-sector company to help implement foreign policy. The recent limits on Ukraine, despite being a US ally, have also rattled officials in Europe, some of whom argue that Europe must develop its own military satellite communications capabilities because no viable short-term alternative currently exists. STARSHIELD RESTRICTIONS HOBBLE UKRAINE MILITARY Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said last week that his country's access to Starshield, the military version of the Starlink system, had been intentionally limited, interfering with the performance of the country’s military drones. He also said the speeds were reduced for Starlink, which Ukraine uses for some military activities including defense against Russian missile attacks. Reuters has reported that [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"the order to throttle Starshield"] came from inside the White House. The Trump administration has acknowledged the slowdown but has not said whether it gave the order. The White House, contacted for comment, referred Reuters to Trump's remarks on Friday, when he said he had not spoken with Musk about Starlink access issues for Ukraine and that "if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out." Halyna Yusypiuk, a spokesperson for the Ukrainian embassy in Washington, said Ukraine's priority is "to have the service restored to normal speed as soon as possible, as the lives of our people depend on it." SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment, although Musk said in a social media post earlier this week: “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately (by the president of the United States).” Democratic US Representative Jason Crow called on Friday for clarity about the recent changes to Ukraine's satellite service, saying there are risks to the US dependence on SpaceX. "Unelected billionaires and private corporations should not decide what is in the best interest of America's national security," Crow said. For Ukraine, the Starlink internet service has become the lifeblood of frontline communication between units, who say there is currently no rival to the capabilities of SpaceX's products. Starshield receivers, largely impervious to radio jamming, are used as onboard guidance systems and to provide links to a remote pilot for Ukrainian drones, including deep behind Russian lines inside Ukraine. MUSK'S INFLUENCE RAISES UNCERTAINTY Musk's role as the strong-willed CEO of a company with outsized influence over US national security has at times raised questions over who is making decisions about SpaceX's satellite services. The SpaceX CEO is "supposed to be a business executive, with government contracts, and he's essentially making huge foreign policy decisions," said Armand Musey, president of Summit Ridge Group, a satellite industry consultancy. "He's sufficiently ambiguous of a person that you don't know if his decisions are sort of his personal quirks, or it's because there's an influence elsewhere that's impacting him," Musey said. In previous years, Musk has moved to limit Ukraine’s access to Starlink. In 2022, according to Reuters reporting , Musk ordered SpaceX personnel to cut Starlink coverage in areas Ukraine was trying to retake, a move that surprised White House officials. Musk has said publicly that he refused a 2022 Ukrainian request to activate his satellite network in Crimea's port city of Sevastopol to aid an attack on Russia's fleet there, saying he feared complicity in a major act of war. The Biden administration at times relied on Musk to help implement policy, five of the former officials said. Biden officials coordinated with SpaceX to thwart US adversaries by cutting the service, and to help allies by expanding Starlink’s availability, they said. They added that discussions between the government and SpaceX, which usually included Pentagon and White House officials, often focused on preventing groups such as the Iranian-linked Houthis in Yemen and Hezbollah in Lebanon from using Starlink terminals. Biden officials several times shared intelligence with SpaceX that indicated that the Houthis and Hezbollah were using diverted Starlink terminals — hardware that made its way to the militants through intermediaries. In October 2023, during fighting between Israel and Hezbollah militants in southern Lebanon, intelligence officials told the White House that individuals linked to Hezbollah could have gained access to Starlink terminals. Officials had similar concerns about the Houthis in Yemen in 2024 during a US air campaign against the Iran-linked group, five of the officials said. In both cases, the administration contacted SpaceX and asked it to identify the terminals and shut them off. At least some of the terminals were deactivated, said two of the officials. In a 2024 submission to the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, SpaceX said it works closely with US government agencies to secure export authorizations where required and to safeguard technology in support of US national security objectives and foreign policy goals. Soon after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Biden officials pushed SpaceX to expand Starlink use for the Ukrainian military, said two of the former officials. In a separate instance, the Biden administration asked SpaceX to turn on Starlink in Iran during a protest movement launched in September 2022 after the death of Mahsa Amini, an Iranian arrested for not wearing her hijab properly, according to one of the former officials. Starlink terminals were moved into the country with the help of the administration, said the official, who declined to say how many were transferred. The Trump administration took a similar step earlier this year and discussed with Musk and SpaceX getting Starlink terminals into Iran and activated following US-Israeli strikes in the country in June 2025 and again in February 2026, a former senior Trump official and a person familiar with the matter told Reuters. Neither the Trump administration nor SpaceX has publicly confirmed that those terminals were turned on. The Wall Street Journal reported in February that the US government had sent thousands of Starlink terminals into Iran. Iran's delegation to the UN did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Marco Rubio calls on those seeking change in Cuba to partner with CIA
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on those seeking change in Cuba to partner with the CIA as President Donald Trump said Washington would "take care of Cuba" after dealing with Iran and send in the top US diplomat to finish the deal.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on those seeking change in Cuba to partner with the CIA as President Donald Trump said Washington would "take care of Cuba" after dealing with Iran and send in the top US diplomat to finish the deal. DETAILS AND QUOTES: "We'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran ... then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal," Trump told a rally in Florida. "To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio, who has been handling much of the Cuba-related policy for Trump, said on X on Friday. Rubio urged those disappointed by Cuba's government to "seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA," without elaborating further. The Trump administration [USN:L1N45L02I TEXT:"has previously stated"] its goal is to change Cuba's communist government. A US-imposed oil blockade implemented earlier this year has put Cuba under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and [USN:L1N44002K TEXT:"blackouts"] exacerbated by failing infrastructure. Washington has maintained an embargo on Cuba for over 60 years. The Trump administration has been [USN:L1N4590T5 TEXT:"stepping up pressure"] on Havana after the US military in January seized then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in a deadly raid. Cuba's foreign minister told the UN General Assembly last month Cuba would always be open for dialogue with Washington. UN rights experts have condemned the oil blockade as a violation of international law while rights advocates say the Trump administration's threats have echoed an [USN:L4N3YE036 TEXT:"imperialist approach"]. Trump [USN:L1N45I044 TEXT:"predicted last month"] the US and Cuba would reach an agreement and that he did not think military action would be necessary.

item.title: Leclerc fastest for Ferrari in US GP Friday practice
item.description: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was a close second ahead of a race that could make him Formula One's youngest champion.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led the way in US Grand Prix practice on Friday, with Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli a close second ahead of a race that could make him Formula One's youngest champion. Leclerc set the pace of one minute 35.291 seconds in a sunny second practice at Austin's Circuit of the Americas after also lapping fastest in the earlier session with a time of 1:36.052 in his upgraded car on a bumpy track. "It has been a very clean Friday for me, but the others seem to be gaining more than us from Friday to Saturday and seeing the little gap there is, it is not going to be so easy tomorrow," he said. Antonelli, the 20-year-old who must win on Sunday to have a first chance of taking the title, was fifth in session one when Red Bull's Max Verstappen was closest to 2024 winner Leclerc. The Italian, who complained about his seat moving, then improved to second place and ended the day 0.042 off the pace. "We didn't have the best FP1 session, with the car balance not in a great place," said Antonelli, who is 102 points clear of closest rival and teammate George Russell. "We were able to improve that for FP2 though and we took a good step forward." HAMILTON NOT COMFORTABLE ON BUMPY TRACK Verstappen, winner in Austin last year, is chasing his third successive victory after Singapore and Malaysia. He ended second practice as the third fastest and 0.189 off Leclerc with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton fourth and Russell fifth. "We tried a different direction with the set-up, but I wasn’t comfortable in the car, especially over the bumps," said Hamilton. "Charles showed there’s pace there, so we need to understand how we can get the car into a better place on my side." Russell had a black-and-white warning flag for an incident with Leclerc that led to the Monegasque going off track early in the second session, but stewards decided against any further action. McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris was third fastest, 0.245 off the pace, in first practice and then seventh later on and behind Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. "I think Lando is definitely a lot quicker than his lap time," McLaren boss Zak Brown told Sky Sports television. "He didn't get his third sector in. His first two sectors were very strong. "So I think we are much quicker than we looked. I think Ferrari's lap time, Mercedes' lap time, there or thereabouts." Norris sounded less sure: "The pace is not bad. We seem a step away from Red Bull and Ferrari, probably Mercedes as well, but the car is very difficult to drive, too difficult to be consistent and get a nice feeling consistently." Teammate Oscar Piastri was eighth fastest, with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar ninth and Haas's Oliver Bearman completing the top 10. Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto all collected grid drops for changes to their power units. Lindblad will drop five places from wherever he qualifies on Saturday, Colapinto 10 places and Bortoleto 20. Williams looked to be struggling, with Carlos Sainz 20th and Alex Albon 22nd in practice two. "The car is a mess right now. It's a mess. I have no confidence in the rear," said Sainz over the team radio.

item.title: India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermining India-UK pact benefits, trade group says
item.description: India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75% tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75% tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters. Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during the years of protracted negotiations leading up to the deal's July 15 implementation, though India ultimately agreed to halve import taxes on certain Scotch imports from 150% to 75% immediately and to 40% over 10 years. The British government said "iconic UK products" like whiskies would benefit from the pact. Indian investigators, however, have privately told companies the reduced rate does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, creating the first significant dispute over the free trade agreement since it took effect. India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence [USN:L4N4650OU TEXT:"searched the offices"] of Pernod (PERP.PA) and Diageo (DGE.L) and questioned executives this month as part of an investigation into whether they misclassified imported products to benefit from the reduced rate. CLASSIFICATION ISSUE RISKS UNDERMINING PACT, GROUP SAYS In a letter to India's commerce minister on Friday, the International Spirits and Wines Association of India wrote that the classification issue "risks undermining, in practice, an important market-access benefit negotiated and agreed between India and the United Kingdom". "The preferential tariff treatment negotiated ... could effectively become unavailable for these imports," continued the letter, a copy of which was seen by Reuters. ISWAI declined to comment on its letter, while India's commerce ministry did not immediately respond. Pernod, which counts India as its biggest market by volume, declined to comment. Diageo did not respond to a request for comment. Both told Reuters earlier this week that they were cooperating with Indian authorities carrying out the investigation. In the British government's first comment on the controversy, a spokesperson said: "We are working with the government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal." Import tariff disputes have long been a [USN:L4N3P10W5 TEXT:"sore point"] for foreign investors in India, who have in the past faced demands for large amounts of back tax. Such disputes have embroiled the likes of Samsung and Volkswagen. Pernod faces antitrust cases in India and a $314 million back-tax demand from Indian authorities, who accuse it of undervaluing some imports. The company denies wrongdoing. BIG IMPLICATIONS FOR INDIA'S DRINKS SECTOR ISWAI's letter underscores the shockwaves the investigation has sent through India's $65 billion alcohol market. Britain accounts for almost 75% of India's imported spirits, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, according to Crisil Ratings. Indian government inspectors have told companies that they do not benefit from the reduced 75% tariff on bulk imports of Scotch concentrates, which must be declared under a customs classification that attracts a 150% duty, three people with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters. Pernod and Diageo import bulk concentrates, mixing them with other ingredients to produce hugely popular Indian brands like Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell’s. The three people said companies including Diageo and Pernod believe concentrates imported from Britain should benefit from the new, lower tariff. ISWAI said in its letter that the India-UK agreement expressly provides preferential tariff treatment for whisky under the relevant tariff lines. An urgent clarification could ensure market-access benefits negotiated by India and Britain are realised "while avoiding uncertainty and disruption for legitimate industry participants", the letter said. On Saturday, the UK-based Scotch Whisky Association told Reuters in a statement that the import of bulk Scotch is key to whisky’s overall success in India and that upholding the core principles of the bilateral pact is vital. The association, which counts Diageo and Pernod's Chivas Brothers as members, added the industry was "committed to working in partnership with the UK and Indian governments on the smooth implementation of the deal", so its benefits are unlocked.

item.title: Seven killed as gunmen open fire at church in Jordan in 'terrorist' attack, authorities say
item.description: It is a rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority that authorities described as a terrorist act.
item.dc:creator: Alaa al-Sukhni
item.content:encoded: Seven people were killed on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan, said the head of the country's Public Security Directorate, in a rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority that authorities described as a terrorist act by extremists. Speaking at a press conference, Major General Abdallah al-Maaytah said most of those wounded in the shooting at the Hamoud Church in Karak governorate were still receiving treatment, and that the hunt for the attackers was ongoing. Jordan's health minister said 40 people were wounded. Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh said the attack had been carried out by "extremists", but that it was too early to tell whether they had any links to known groups inside or outside Jordan. Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan, which is relatively stable, though authorities in the US ally say that in recent years they have repeatedly foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants. There was no immediate claim of responsibility. A video aired on Jordan's state-owned Al-Mamlaka television station that appeared to be from a security camera on the church showed three people firing at it from a sidewalk and hiding behind trees and a low wall. The video showed the attackers then running towards the church's entrance. Reuters was able to verify the video from the entry path and wall surrounding the church, as well as other details. "This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and we will not allow society to go down this path," Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said in a post on X. Khaled Burqan, who was at the funeral, told Al-Mamlaka that dozens of people were present and the gunmen opened fire on them for several minutes. Ihab Ammareen, another witness, told the station he saw bloodied people collapse on the floor after the attack. "People were crying, wailing, screaming — it's hard to describe," he said. BLOOD SMEARED ON THE GROUND Jordan's King Abdullah, a major US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist". "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation. Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity," he said in a statement. Reuters footage from the church after the attack showed blood smeared on the floor near its entrance, where security forces were deployed. In a post on X, United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the violence and said attacks against civilians and places of worship are unacceptable. People who gathered at a Karak government hospital to support the wounded expressed shock. "What happened today has left people unable to speak or raise our voices. But our only reproach to the state is that it must investigate these dark ideas — where they come from and how they enter the minds of our children," said one of them, Hani Al-Mbaydeen. Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world. The US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz described it on X as a "depraved and brutal attack on a house of worship." Jordan was among the US allies in the region to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.
